candidates.bio: 2 Versatile is a Canadian old-school hip-hop act whose self-titled album appeared in 1994. The group is part of the early Canadian rap catalogue and is associated with recordings including Cuddle with Me, which features Canadian R&B singer Glenn Lewis. Northern Dial carries 2 Versatile as part of that 1990s Canadian hip-hop lineage.
Toronto producer and multi-instrumentalist 2nd Son makes soul-, funk-, R&B- and hip-hop-informed music and is known for a long-running creative partnership with Canadian singer a l l i e.

Formed in the Vancouver area in the early 1980s, 54•40 grew out of Canada's college-rock and post-punk underground before becoming one of the country's most durable alternative-rock bands. Led by singer-guitarist Neil Osborne with bassist Brad Merritt as a long-running core member, the group developed from wiry, politically alert early records into a broader guitar sound that could move between jangle, roots rock and muscular radio rock. The 1987 album Show Me marked a major national breakthrough, while songs such as "One Gun" and "One Day in Your Life" established the band well beyond its West Coast beginnings.

The 1990s turned 54•40 into a Canadian radio institution. Dear Dear, Smilin' Buddha Cabaret and Trusted by Millions all reached platinum status in Canada, with songs including "Nice to Luv You," "Ocean Pearl" and "Lies to Me" becoming fixtures of the era. Their 1986 song "I Go Blind" also gained a second life when Hootie & the Blowfish recorded it, introducing Osborne's writing to a much larger U.S. audience. Rather than being defined by one crossover moment, however, 54•40 built its reputation through consistency across albums, touring and a deep catalogue of Canadian rock-radio staples.

That longevity is central to the band's significance. 54•40 has remained active across more than four decades, moving from independent post-punk roots into mainstream Canadian rock without losing the songwriting identity that connected those eras. Later records such as Yes to Everything, Lost in the City and West Coast Band kept the group recording well beyond its commercial peak, making 54•40 a useful bridge between Canada's 1980s alternative underground and the national rock infrastructure that flourished in the 1990s.

646yf4t, pronounced Babyfat, is Oshawa, Ontario singer, songwriter and producer Zachary Simmonds. The younger brother of Daniel Caesar, he moved from production into his own genre-blurring blend of alternative R&B, punk and soul with the 2025 project Growing Pains before appearing on Caesar's Son of Spergy.

8485 is a Toronto-rooted singer, songwriter and producer who emerged from the internet-native experimental pop scene around 2020. After an earlier background playing in post-hardcore bands, she moved toward electronic production and became associated with the Helix Tears collective, working closely with fellow Canadian producer Blackwinterwells. Early releases such as alpha testing and the plague town EP established a sound that could move between hyperpop's digital abrasion and more vulnerable synth-pop songwriting.

That online scene made 8485 a frequent collaborator across a generation of experimental pop and digicore artists. Her work has intersected with Blackwinterwells, midwxst, underscores, Anamanaguchi and others, placing a Canadian voice inside a movement whose communities developed as much through Discord, SoundCloud and remote file-sharing as through conventional local scenes.

The 2023 album Personal Protocol pushed that approach into a more sustained album format, while software gore continued her interest in distorted digital textures. Her later collaboration with Danny Brown further demonstrated how the internet-pop vocabulary she helped develop could cross into established alternative hip-hop. 8485 matters in the Northern Dial catalogue as part of a distinctly 2020s Canadian story: an artist whose scene is geographically Toronto-rooted but culturally international and online-first.
Toronto-born rapper and singer 8OND makes melodic Canadian hip-hop shaped by atmospheric hooks, laid-back production and a grassroots performance career built in the city.

A Girl Named Sue is the solo project of Montréal-born artist and producer Charlie Kunce-Belhadj. Working independently and handling her own production, she has built a catalogue that moves through atmospheric electronic pop, drum and bass and emotionally understated songwriting rather than staying within a single genre lane.

The project expanded through a run of collaborative and solo releases in 2025 and 2026, including the Moonsoak EP, "April," "Ma Chance" and "All U Need." Collaborations with artists including Tora and IMANU helped place her voice inside a wider electronic network, while "Ma Chance" also reached francophone Canadian radio and chart contexts.

For Northern Dial, A Girl Named Sue is an example of a Montréal artist whose career is developing through self-production and international electronic collaboration rather than a conventional band or singer-songwriter route. The catalogue is still young, but the combination of independent production, bilingual context and fast-moving electronic work makes the project worth documenting early.

Toronto R&B singer-songwriter ABBI WOODS draws on her upbringing in the city and her Ethiopian and Eritrean roots to make intimate, emotionally ambivalent music about identity, relationships and self-discovery. She emerged in 2025 with singles including HBD, Scattered Bodies and TOO LATE, building a contemporary soul sound around candid writing and atmospheric production.

ACHEL is a Quebec francophone artist working across contemporary pop and rap-adjacent sounds. His catalogue includes collaborations with artists including Peypo, lilaash, popo and Madior, and he is documented by MUSIQC, Quebec's francophone music discovery platform. Northern Dial carries ACHEL as part of its contemporary Quebec catalogue.

Ada Lea is the recording project of Montréal songwriter, musician and visual artist Alexandra Levy. Her 2019 debut, what we say in private, introduced a diaristic strain of indie rock in which intimate songwriting and Levy's visual-art practice inform one another. The 2020 EP woman, here extended that world while beginning a collaboration with producer and engineer Marshall Vore.

Levy widened the frame on 2021's one hand on the steering wheel the other sewing a garden, a record built from stories and memories mapped onto Montréal. She began writing the material during an artist residency in Banff before recording in Los Angeles with Vore and collaborators including Harrison Whitford and Tasy Hudson. The result moved between folk, soft rock and art-pop while keeping place, memory and narrative at the centre of the songs.

After the archival 2024 EP notes, Ada Lea returned with when i paint my masterpiece, recorded largely live in rural Ontario with producer Luke Temple. Its acoustic, ensemble-driven approach connected her work to older Canadian folk traditions without abandoning the imaginative storytelling that defines the project. Across those records, Levy has built a distinctly Montréal body of work that treats songs less as isolated singles than as pieces of larger emotional and geographic worlds.

Toronto-born singer-songwriter Adam Klobi is a Canadian alternative artist whose emotionally direct writing and resonant vocals first found a large audience through viral online covers. After beginning to pursue music seriously in his hometown, he signed with Darkroom Records and built an original catalogue around releases including Rain, RUT, Piece of Mind and YESTERDAY, TODAY.

Admiral Naughtz is a Toronto underground hip-hop MC associated with the city's hardcore and boom-bap scene and the Hella Treez circle. Active on Toronto bills for years, he has collaborated with D.O.V and DJ Chino420; his feature on D.O.V's Back From The Dead is the Northern Dial library credit, while U.G.M.L. extends that affiliation into Hella Treez's current catalogue.

Adriiana is Italian-born Canadian pop singer Adriana Lombardo, a Toronto artist who began performing as a child before appearing on YTV's The Next Star. Her early singles earned national attention through Canadian radio and television placements, and she later joined Canadian independent label Wax Records while continuing to develop a dance-pop and R&B-influenced catalogue.

Afrolistic is a Toronto hip-hop artist associated with the late-1990s Circle collective around Choclair, Kardinal Offishall and Saukrates. He appears on Choclair's What It Takes (Ill B. Mix) and is part of the city's foundational independent rap era. Northern Dial carries Afrolistic as part of its Canadian hip-hop archive.

Aïda is a Montreal-based Canadian singer-songwriter whose music blends pop, R&B and multicultural influences with a bilingual Frenglish identity. Rooted in Montreal's diverse music scene and African heritage, her work moves across languages and styles while centring a contemporary Quebec perspective. Northern Dial carries Aïda as part of Montreal's independent vocal scene.
Venezuelan-Canadian singer-songwriter and producer Aiona Santana blends Latin pop, R&B and contemporary urban music with Venezuelan rhythms and multilingual songwriting.

Alex K is a Toronto-based DJ and producer known as one half of Delirious & Alex K. The duo has produced official remixes for artists including Justin Bieber, Dua Lipa, Major Lazer, Pitbull and Sean Paul while building a club-focused catalogue rooted in Toronto. Northern Dial carries Alex K as part of Canada's electronic and remix culture.

Alexander Gallant is a Halifax-area folk singer-songwriter known for fingerpicked guitar, dark humour and sharply observed storytelling. Part of the creative community around 45 Portland Street in Dartmouth, he has released projects including Waiting Table Blues, Rubber Monster Suit and The Prince of Birchy Head.

Allie is the library credit for Toronto R&B singer-songwriter Allison Ho-Sang, who records as a l l i e. Her atmospheric blend of soul, electronic music and pop has earned SOCAN Songwriting Prize recognition, a Polaris Music Prize longlist and a JUNO nomination, while collaborations include Illa J and Canadian production duo Potatohead People on Sunflower.

Alsham is a Toronto underground hip-hop artist represented on the 1998 local compilation Invading the Mega City. Northern Dial carries 'Invasion' and 'Mega Garden,' the latter featuring Black U Sun and K.P. The compilation documents Toronto's independent rap scene at the end of the 1990s.

Ambeez is an alternate recording name used by Halifax rapper and producer Ambition, a longtime member of Nova Scotia's independent hip-hop community and the wider Backburner collective. His catalogue includes solo work, collaborations with Uncle Fester and later releases as one half of The Library Steps with Jesse Dangerously.

Amber Days is a Montréal indie pop-rock quartet made up of Mario Gervais, Alexy Préfontaine, Samuel Jalbert and Vincent Dessureault. Formerly known as Alpha & the Van, the group adopted the Amber Days name in 2024 and established itself on the Montréal and Québec live-music scene. Northern Dial carries 'Present Tense', the opening track on the band's 2026 debut album On The Run.

Halifax rapper and producer Ambition, also known as Ambeez, is part of Nova Scotia's long-running independent hip-hop community and the wider Backburner collective. He has worked closely with Uncle Fester, released solo projects including Man of the Year and later formed The Library Steps with Jesse Dangerously.

Montréal-based Anachnid is an Oji-Cree and Mi'kmaq multidisciplinary artist whose electronic music, visual identity and storytelling draw directly from Indigenous experience without reducing it to a single genre or message. Raised largely in Atikamekw territory in western Québec, she developed a performance language that moves between experimental pop, electronic production and Indigenous cultural reference. Her early singles, including "Windigo" and "Sky Woman," introduced an artist comfortable turning traditional stories, contemporary urban life and personal mythology into the same sonic world.

Her 2020 debut album Dreamweaver brought that work to a wider Canadian audience. The album was longlisted for the Polaris Music Prize and earned Félix nominations, while Anachnid's songwriting and performance work also received recognition from the Indigenous Music Awards. In 2021, she won the Félix for Indigenous Artist of the Year, confirming her as one of the more distinctive Indigenous voices in Québec's contemporary music scene. Songs from Dreamweaver balance atmospheric electronic production with direct writing about identity, violence, spirituality and survival, making the record feel both personal and politically aware without becoming didactic.

Anachnid's significance lies in how naturally she connects scenes that are often kept separate: Indigenous music, Montréal experimental pop and electronic production. Rather than presenting tradition and modernity as opposites, her work treats them as part of the same living identity. Later releases including "Freak of Nature" and 2026's "Happy Birthday" have kept that approach active, while her broader multidisciplinary practice reinforces the sense that Anachnid is building a world around the music rather than simply a catalogue of songs.
Vancouver rapper Anami Vice is a Canadian hip-hop artist known for melodic, pop-aware rap and independent releases tied to the West Coast scene.
Montréal singer-songwriter Anaïs Cardot makes intimate French-language soul and R&B, pairing warm vocals with emotionally direct writing.
Toronto singer and songwriter anders makes contemporary R&B with a moody, melodic sound closely associated with the city's late-night scene.
Toronto-born R&B singer-songwriter Andreena Miller, formerly known as Andreena Mill, has been part of the city's contemporary soul and R&B scene since her teens.

Andrew Ranxx is the earlier recording name of Toronto-raised reggae singer and deejay Andrew White, now known as Akustix. Born in St. Elizabeth, Jamaica and raised in Toronto, he became part of Canada's reggae scene in the 1990s, later earning a JUNO nomination as Akustix and continuing to record and write reggae music.

Angel Duss is a Toronto hip-hop vocalist and rapper connected to the city's 7Bills and Ghetto Concept scene. Her credits include multiple appearances on Ghetto Concept releases, including N.E.W.S., Krazy Mixed Up World, Blades of Ice and later recordings. Northern Dial carries Angel Duss as part of its archival Toronto hip-hop catalogue.

Angela Apigo is an Ontario vocalist and songwriter active in Canadian R&B, soul and hip-hop collaborations. Her recorded work includes featured vocals on Big Jacks' Sunflower EP and Kutcorners' Round & Round, with credits connected to Toronto's independent soul and beat scene. Northern Dial carries Angela Apigo as part of its Canadian R&B and collaborator catalogue.

Kitchener-born Angelica Appelman is a Canadian country singer-songwriter based in Stratford, Ontario. Her contemporary country sound draws on the 1990s artists she grew up with while pairing hook-driven production with personal storytelling across releases including A Reason or A Season and Half Hearted.

Oakville, Ontario singer-songwriter Anjulie Persaud emerged in the late 2000s with a pop sound shaped by R&B, electronic production and the reggae and calypso she heard growing up in an Indo-Guyanese household. Her 2009 debut album introduced "Boom," a sleek, percussion-driven single that brought her early television and radio exposure and established her as a Canadian pop artist with a strong songwriting identity. She followed with singles including "Brand New Chick" and "You and I," moving further toward dance-pop while retaining the rhythmic instincts that distinguished her from much of the country's singer-songwriter mainstream.

"Brand New Chick" became one of her largest Canadian hits, reaching the Top 20 of the Canadian Hot 100, earning platinum certification and receiving a 2012 JUNO nomination for Dance Recording of the Year. Anjulie's career also expanded well beyond her own catalogue. She built a parallel reputation as a songwriter, contributing to material recorded by artists including Kelly Clarkson, Nicki Minaj, Cassie and Icona Pop and collaborating across pop and electronic music with producers and artists such as Zedd, Diplo and Benny Benassi.

That dual role is what gives Anjulie an important place in modern Canadian pop. Her own recordings connected the late-2000s singer-songwriter world to the EDM-heavy pop that followed, while her behind-the-scenes writing placed a Canadian voice inside a much larger international hit-making network. She has continued releasing independently and collaborating across electronic and alternative pop, making her career less about one sustained commercial era than about adaptability across songwriting, performance and production-driven pop culture.

ANJXLXE (Anne-Julie) is a Montreal-based singer-songwriter whose music bridges contemporary R&B, soul and pop in French and English. Her debut album ANJXLXE arrived in 2025, earning an ADISQ nomination for R&B/Soul Album of the Year, while singles including Old School Love and Destin helped establish her within Quebec's modern R&B scene. Northern Dial carries ANJXLXE as part of its contemporary Montreal R&B catalogue.

Anthony Bezel is a Toronto-area artist and producer working across hip-hop and contemporary R&B. Based in Mississauga and active within the Greater Toronto Area, he has released solo music and collaborations with artists from the region's independent scene. Northern Dial carries Anthony Bezel as part of its GTA hip-hop catalogue.

Toronto MC and radio host Arcee is a veteran of Canada's independent hip-hop scene, known for sharp battle-oriented lyricism and for co-hosting the influential Real Frequency show on CKLN. His early singles and collaborations with producers including Da Grassroots, DJ Serious and Jake One were collected on the MixedWell mixtape, while his catalogue also includes appearances alongside Brassmunk, IRS, King Reign and other Toronto artists.

Aristo is the recording name of Brione Wishart, a South America-born artist raised in Toronto's west end. He began writing and recording while still in school, later building an independent hip-hop career that included touring and releases such as Top of the World. Playa 4 Life from that project is his Northern Dial library credit.
Winnipeg duo Ash Koley pairs vocalist Ashley Koley with guitarist and keyboardist Phil Deschambault in bright Canadian new wave and alternative pop.

asia is a Toronto underground hip-hop artist represented on the 1998 local compilation Invading the Mega City. Northern Dial carries the artist's track 'Dedicated' from that release. The compilation was built around Toronto-based independent rap artists and documents the city's late-1990s hip-hop scene.

Astrokidjay is a Tanzania-born, Brampton-based rapper and singer whose melodic sound moves between hip-hop, R&B, trap and Afrobeats. His 2019 single Ibiza helped break him out of the local scene, and he has since become a recognizable voice in the Greater Toronto Area's new generation of rap artists. Northern Dial carries his music as part of its contemporary Canadian hip-hop catalogue.

Edmonton-formed Canadian dance-pop group Audio Playground combines electronic club production with pop and R&B vocals and has released multilingual dance singles for Canadian and international audiences.

Avenoir is a Canadian R&B singer and songwriter raised in Edmonton, Alberta. Born in South Africa, he built his sound around piano-led, atmospheric progressive R&B and earned a JUNO nomination for his 2023 EP Noire before releasing his debut album Mirage in 2025. Northern Dial carries Avenoir as part of its contemporary Canadian R&B catalogue.

Avril is a split library credit for Canadian singer-songwriter Avril Lavigne on the 2020 ArtistsCAN charity recording of Lean on Me. The Napanee-raised pop-rock star joined more than two dozen Canadian artists for the Sony Music Canada release supporting Canadian Red Cross COVID-19 relief.

Palestinian-Canadian singer, songwriter and producer Merna Bishouty first released music under the name Ayah before continuing her career as Merna. After settling in Toronto, she built a soulful R&B catalogue that included collaborations with DJ Jazzy Jeff, Slakah the Beatchild and Toronto rapper Adam Bomb.

AYOO BIGZ is a Toronto underground rapper whose career stretches from early mixtapes made on a karaoke machine to a return to recording after a long hiatus. Rooted in East Toronto hip-hop, his hard-edged catalogue includes collaborations with Canadian artists such as Merkules, Sayzee, Daniel Son and Tona as well as international underground rap veterans.
Vancouver pop-rap artist B00sted, born Keegan Jaeckel, blends hip-hop flows with melodic pop and alternative-rock influences in a growing West Coast Canadian catalogue.

Baby Chilli is a Toronto-raised, Vancouver-based alternative artist, guitarist and producer. After growing up around Toronto's music scene, he relocated to Vancouver and has worked from the city's independent scene as a solo artist and collaborator, including releases such as Sweet Tooth and MUSTANG and work with Vancouver singer-songwriter Matt Storm and DACEY.
Nova Scotia-born singer-songwriter Baby Nova, born Kayleigh O'Connor, makes dramatic Canadian dream-pop and alternative pop built around cinematic production and emotionally exposed writing.
Kitchener-born Canadian singer-songwriter, producer and multi-instrumentalist BAD CHILD, born Isaiah Steinberg, makes genre-blurring alternative pop shaped by hip-hop, rock and electronic production.

BALAM KIEL is a Toronto-based Spanish artist whose music blends reggaeton, Latin pop and hip-hop. He has built a solo catalogue including Capítulo Uno while collaborating with Canadian artists such as Snow and Cole James. His appearances with Snow on Reason to Love and Together are the two BALAM KIEL credits in the Northern Dial library.
